guide.title: Oxygen Therapy
guide.lead: Oxygen is a drug, so give it to a target rather than to everyone. Aim for 94–98%, or 88–92% if the patient is at risk of CO₂ retention. Never withhold it from a critically hypoxic patient.

sections.title: Targets
rows: At risk of CO₂ retention (e.g. COPD)
Normal SpO₂ and not breathless (e.g. uncomplicated chest pain, stroke)
notes: Critically hypoxic COPD patient: treat the hypoxia first, then titrate down to 88–92%, watching rate and mental status.

sections.title: Choose the device
rows: Mild hypoxia; won't tolerate a mask
Moderate hypoxia (at least 6 L/min to flush CO₂)
Severe hypoxia; keep the reservoir inflated
Inadequate or absent breathing: it ventilates

sections.title: Safety
items: Oxygen feeds fire: no smoking or open flame nearby.
Cylinders are under high pressure: secure them and protect the valve.

quiz.explanation: BTS target for most acutely ill patients.

quiz.q: COPD patient in mild distress, SpO₂ 90%. Target?
Why must a simple face mask run at least 6 L/min?
options: To flush exhaled CO₂ out of the mask
quiz.explanation: Below that the patient rebreathes CO₂.

quiz.q: An alert chest pain patient has SpO₂ 97% on room air. Oxygen?
options: High-flow NRB for all chest pain

quiz.q: Critically hypoxic COPD patient, SpO₂ 78%. What do you do?
options: Withhold oxygen to protect the drive
quiz.explanation: Never withhold oxygen from life-threatening hypoxia.

quiz.q: The NRB reservoir collapses fully on each breath. Fix?
options: Increase the flow until it stays inflated

flashcards.question: Target with risk of CO₂ retention (COPD)
Non-rebreather
flashcards.answer: 10–15 L/min, about 60–90%; keep the reservoir inflated.

flashcards.question: Simple face mask minimum flow
flashcards.answer: At least 6 L/min, to flush exhaled CO₂.

flashcards.question: Oxygen hazards
flashcards.answer: Supports combustion; cylinders are high pressure: secure them, no flame.

flashcards.question: Critically hypoxic COPD
flashcards.answer: Never withhold: treat the hypoxia, then titrate to 88–92%.

flashcards.question: Normal SpO₂ and not breathless
flashcards.answer: No supplemental oxygen (e.g. uncomplicated chest pain or stroke).

critical.scenario: A COPD patient (SpO₂ 86%) is put on an NRB at 15 L/min. Minutes later he is drowsy with a slowing respiratory rate.
critical.question: Concern and action?

options.t: CO₂ retention from too much oxygen: titrate to 88–92% and be ready to ventilate

options.f: Drowsiness and slowing rate are danger signs.

critical.kpi: Titrates oxygen and monitors ventilation in COPD

critical.scenario: A critically ill trauma patient (SpO₂ 80%) is on an NRB, but the reservoir collapses with every breath.
critical.question: What's wrong?

options.t: Flow too low: increase until the reservoir stays inflated

options.f: The bag should stay partly inflated.

critical.kpi: Recognizes and corrects inadequate NRB flow

critical.scenario: An alert chest pain patient has SpO₂ 97% on room air. A colleague wants high-flow oxygen 'because it's a heart attack'.
critical.question: Best approach?

options.t: Nasal cannula at 6 L/min for all chest pain

critical.explanation: Give oxygen to a target, not by reflex.
critical.kpi: Avoids unnecessary oxygen in a normoxic patient
